questions.text: Let $\mathrm{A}=\{\mathrm{x} \in \mathrm{R}:|\mathrm{x}+1|<2\}$ and $B=\{x \in R:|x-1| \geq 2\}$. Then which one of the following statements is NOT true ?

options.D:
$\mathrm{A} \cup \mathrm{B}=\mathrm{R}-[1,3)$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. A: $\mathrm{x} \in(-3,1) \quad \mathrm{B}: \mathrm{x} \in(-\infty,-1] \cup[3, \infty)$
$$\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{A}=(-\infty,-3] \cup[3, \infty)=\mathrm{R}-(-3,3)$$

questions.text: Let $a, b \in R$ be such that the equation $\mathrm{ax}^{2}-2 \mathrm{bc}+15=0$ has a repeated root $\alpha$. If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2}-2 b x+21=0$, then $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}$ is equal to:

options.D:
92

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol. $a x^{2}-2 b x+15=0$
$$\begin{array}{l}
2 \alpha=\frac{2 b}{a}, \alpha^{2}=\frac{15}{a} \\
\frac{\alpha}{2}=\frac{15}{2 b} \\
\alpha=\frac{15}{b} \\
x^{2}-2 b x+21=0 \\
\left(\frac{15}{b}\right)^{2}-2 b\left(\frac{15}{b}\right)+21=0 \\
b^{2}=25 \\
\alpha+\beta=2 b, \alpha \beta=21 \\
\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=4 b^{2}-42 \\
=58
\end{array}$$

questions.text: Let $\mathrm{z}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{z}_{2}$ be two complex numbers such that $\overline{\mathrm{z}}_{1}=\mathrm{i} \overline{\mathrm{z}}_{2}$ and $\arg \left(\frac{\mathrm{z}_{1}}{\overline{\mathrm{z}}_{2}}\right)=\pi$. Then

options.D:
$\arg \mathrm{z}_{1}=-\frac{3 \pi}{4}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. $\overline{\mathrm{z}}_{1}=\mathrm{iz}_{2}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{z}_{1}=-\mathrm{iz}_{2} \\
\arg \left(\frac{\mathrm{z}_{1}}{\overline{\mathrm{z}_{2}}}\right)=\pi
\end{array}$$
$$\arg \left(\mathrm{z}_{2}\right)=\theta$$
$$2 \theta=\frac{3 \pi}{2}$$
$\arg \left(\mathrm{z}_{2}\right)=\theta=\frac{3 \pi}{4}, \arg \mathrm{z}_{1}=\frac{\pi}{4}$

questions.text: $\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}}\left(\tan ^{2} x\left(\left(2 \sin ^{2} x+3 \sin x+4\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}-\left(\sin ^{2} x+6 \sin x+2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right)$ is equal to

options.D:
$-\frac{1}{6}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \tan ^{2} x\left[\sqrt{2 \sin ^{2} x+3 \sin x+4}-\sqrt{\sin ^{2} x+6 \sin x+2}\right]= \\
\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\tan ^{2} x\left[\sin ^{2} x-3 \sin x+2\right]}{\sqrt{9}+\sqrt{9}} \\
\quad=\lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\tan ^{2} x(\sin x-1)(\sin x-2)}{6} \\
\quad=\frac{1}{6} \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \tan ^{2} x(1-\sin x) \\
\quad=\frac{1}{6} \lim _{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sin ^{2} x(1-\sin x)}{(1-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}=\frac{1}{12}
\end{array}$$

questions.text: The area of the region enclosed between the parabolas $\mathrm{y}^{2}=2 \mathrm{x}-1$ and $\mathrm{y}^{2}=4 \mathrm{x}-3$ is

options.D:
$\frac{3}{4}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. Required area $=2 \int_{0}^{1}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}^{2}+3}{4}-\frac{\mathrm{y}^{2}+1}{2}\right) \mathrm{dy}$
$$=2 \int_{0}^{1} \frac{1-\mathrm{y}^{2}}{4} \mathrm{dy}=\frac{1}{2}\left|\mathrm{y}-\frac{\mathrm{y}^{3}}{3}\right|_{0}^{1}=\frac{1}{3}$$

questions.text:
The coefficient of $\mathrm{x}^{101}$ in the expression
$$(5+x)^{500}+x(5+x)^{499}+x^{2}(5+x)^{498}+\ldots . . x^{500}$$
$\mathrm{x}>0$, is

options.D:
${ }^{500} \mathrm{C}_{101}(5)^{399}$

Official Ans. by NTA (A)
Ans. (A)
Sol. $(5+\mathrm{x})^{500}+\mathrm{x}(5+\mathrm{x})^{499}+\mathrm{x}^{2}(5+\mathrm{x})^{498}+\ldots .+\mathrm{x}^{500}$
$$=\frac{(5+x)^{501}-x^{501}}{(5+x)-x}=\frac{(5+x)^{501}-x^{501}}{5}$$

⇒ coefficient $\mathrm{x}^{101}$ in given expression
$$=\frac{{ }^{501} \mathrm{C}_{101} 5^{400}}{5}={ }^{501} \mathrm{C}_{101} 5^{399}$$

questions.text: The sum $1+2 \cdot 3+3 \cdot 3^{2}+$ $\_\_\_\_$ $+10 \cdot 3^{9}$ is equal to

options.D:
$\frac{9 \cdot 3^{10}+1}{2}$

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{S}=1 \cdot 3^{0}+2 \cdot 3^{1}+3 \cdot 3^{2}+\ldots \ldots+10.3^{9} \\
3 \mathrm{~S}=1 \cdot 3^{1}+2.3^{2} \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots+9 \times 3^{9}+10 \times 3^{10} \\

questions.text: A circle touches both the y-axis and the line $\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{y}=0$. Then the locus of its center is

options.D:
$\mathrm{x}^{2}-\mathrm{y}^{2}=2 \mathrm{xy}$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)

Sol. Let (h, k) is centre of circle
$$\begin{array}{l}
\left|\frac{\mathrm{h}-\mathrm{k}}{\sqrt{2}}\right|=|\mathrm{h}| \\
\mathrm{k}^{2}-\mathrm{h}^{2}+2 \mathrm{hk}=0
\end{array}$$
∴ Equation of locus is $\mathrm{y}^{2}-\mathrm{x}^{2}+2 \mathrm{xy}=0$

questions.text: Water is being filled at the rate of $1 \mathrm{~cm}^{3} / \mathrm{sec}$ in a right circular conical vessel (vertex downwards) of height 35 cm and diameter 14 cm. When the height of the water level is 10 cm, the rate (in $\mathrm{cm}^{2} / \mathrm{sec}$ ) at which the wet conical surface area of the vessel increases is

options.D:
$\frac{\sqrt{26}}{10}$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)
Sol. From figure $\frac{\mathrm{r}}{\mathrm{h}}=\frac{7}{35} \Rightarrow \mathrm{~h}=5 \mathrm{r}$

Given $\frac{\mathrm{dV}}{\mathrm{dt}}=1 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{~d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(\frac{\pi \mathrm{r}^{2} \mathrm{~h}}{3}\right)=1$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{dt}}\left(\frac{5 \pi}{3} \mathrm{r}^{3}\right)=1 \Rightarrow \mathrm{r}^{2} \frac{\mathrm{dr}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{1}{5 \pi}$$

Let wet conical surface area $=\mathrm{S}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\pi \mathrm{r} \ell=\pi \mathrm{r} \sqrt{\mathrm{~h}^{2}+\mathrm{r}^{2}} \\
=\sqrt{26} \pi \mathrm{r}^{2} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dt}}=2 \sqrt{26} \pi \mathrm{r} \frac{\mathrm{dr}}{\mathrm{dt}}
\end{array}$$

When $\mathrm{h}=10$ then $\mathrm{r}=2 \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dS}}{\mathrm{dt}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{26}}{10}$

questions.text: If $\mathrm{b}_{\mathrm{n}}=\int_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\cos ^{2} \mathrm{nx}}{\sin \mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}, \mathrm{n} \in \mathrm{N}$, then

options.A: $b_{3}-b_{2}, b_{4}-b_{3}, b_{5}-b_{4}$ are in an A.P. with common difference -2
options.B: $\frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{3}-\mathrm{b}_{2}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{4}-\mathrm{b}_{3}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{5}-\mathrm{b}_{4}}$ are in an A.P. with common difference 2
options.D:
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{3}-\mathrm{b}_{2}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{4}-\mathrm{b}_{3}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{5}-\mathrm{b}_{4}}$ are in an A.P. with common difference -2

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol. $\mathrm{b}_{\mathrm{n}}=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{1+\cos 2 \mathrm{nx}}{\sin \mathrm{x}} \mathrm{dx}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
b_{n+1}-b_{n}=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{\cos ^{2}(n+1) x-\cos ^{2} n x}{\sin x} d x \\
=\int_{0}^{\pi / 2} \frac{-\sin (2 n+1) x \sin x}{\sin x} d x \\
=\left(\frac{\cos (2 n+1) x}{2 n+1}\right)_{0}^{\pi / 2}=\frac{-1}{2 n+1}
\end{array}$$
$\frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{3}-\mathrm{b}_{2}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{4}-\mathrm{b}_{3}}, \frac{1}{\mathrm{~b}_{5}-\mathrm{b}_{4}}$ are in A.P. with c.d. $=-2$

questions.text: If $y=y(x)$ is the solution of the differential equation $2 \mathrm{x}^{2} \frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}-2 \mathrm{xy}+3 \mathrm{y}^{2}=0$ such that $y(e)=\frac{e}{3}$, then $y(1)$ is equal to

options.D:
3

Official Ans. by NTA (B)
Ans. (B)

Sol. $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}-\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}=-\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)^{2} \quad \mathrm{y}=\mathrm{vx}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\frac{\mathrm{dv}}{\mathrm{v}^{2}}=-\frac{3 \mathrm{dx}}{2 \mathrm{x}} \\
-\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}}=-\frac{3}{2} \ln |\mathrm{x}|+\mathrm{C} \\
-\frac{\mathrm{x}}{\mathrm{y}}=\frac{-3}{2} \ln |\mathrm{x}|+\mathrm{C} \\
\mathrm{x}=\mathrm{e}, \mathrm{y}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{3} \\
\mathrm{C}=-\frac{3}{2} \\
\text { When } \mathrm{x}=1, \mathrm{y}=\frac{2}{3}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
If the angle made by the tangent at the point $\left(\mathrm{x}_{0}, \mathrm{y}_{0}\right)$ on the curve $\mathrm{x}=12(\mathrm{t}+\sin \mathrm{t} \cos \mathrm{t})$,
$\mathrm{y}=12(1+\sin \mathrm{t})^{2}, 0<\mathrm{t}<\frac{\pi}{2}$, with the positive x -axis is $\frac{\pi}{3}$, then $\mathrm{y}_{0}$ is equal to

options.D:
48

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (3)
Sol. $\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{2(1+\sin \mathrm{t}) \times \cos \mathrm{t}}{1+\cos 2 \mathrm{t}}$
$$\begin{array}{l}
\Rightarrow \frac{2(1+\sin t) \cos t}{2 \cos ^{2} t}=\sqrt{3} \\
\Rightarrow t=\frac{\pi}{6}, y_{0}=27
\end{array}$$

questions.text: A biased die is marked with numbers 2,4, 8, 16, 32, 32 on its faces and the probability of getting a face with mark n is $\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}}$. If the die is thrown thrice, then the probability, that the sum of the numbers obtained is 48, is

options.D:
$\frac{13}{2^{12}}$

Official Ans. by NTA (D)
Ans. (D)
Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{n})=\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}} \\
\mathrm{P}(2)=\frac{1}{2} \quad \mathrm{P}(8)=\frac{1}{8} \\
\mathrm{P}(4)=\frac{1}{4} \quad \mathrm{P}(16)=\frac{1}{16} \\
\mathrm{P}(32)=\frac{2}{32}
\end{array}$$

Possible cases
16, 16, 16 and 32, 8, 8
Probability $=\frac{1}{16^{3}}+\frac{2}{32} \times \frac{1}{8} \times \frac{1}{8} \times 3=\frac{13}{16^{3}}$

questions.text: The negation of the Boolean expression $((\sim \mathrm{q}) \wedge \mathrm{p}) \Rightarrow((\sim \mathrm{p}) \vee \mathrm{q})$ is logically equivalent to

options.D:
$\sim(\mathrm{q} \Rightarrow \mathrm{p})$

Official Ans. by NTA (C)
Ans. (C)

Sol.
$$\begin{array}{l}
\sim \mathrm{p} \vee \mathrm{q} \equiv \mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q} \\
\sim \mathrm{q} \wedge \mathrm{p} \equiv \sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q})
\end{array}$$

Negation of $\sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q})$
is $\sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q}) \wedge(\sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q}))$ i.e. $\sim(\mathrm{p} \rightarrow \mathrm{q})$
